_notes.general: Every string becomes InDesign text. Use \n inside table cells or callout lines for a forced line break. No em dashes.
_notes.parcels_geojson: File in the work folder from parcels.py. Omit to show a pin instead of outlines.
_notes.stat_labels: Optional. e.g. {"sf": "Enclosed + Covered Area"} when covered storage is included.
_notes.cover_point_size: Optional. Defaults to 30 for short addresses, 26 for long ones.
_notes.aerial_callouts: Optional. parcel = 'all' or the 0-based index of a feature in parcels_geojson. side = left/right.
_notes.buildings: Optional Building Summary page: heads, colw (sum 708.6), rows, total, site [[label, value, label, value], ...], note.
_notes.comps: Any order; the build sorts newest first. Needs lat/lon for the map. photo_src = image file in the work folder.
_notes.comp_fields: Rows of the matrix as [label, key]. Keys refer to fields on each comp.
_notes.pricing: ask / trade totals in dollars (or $/RSF/yr when mode is 'lease'); sf_basis defaults to building_sf. Optional placeholder text. Omit pricing to show $TBD.
_notes.brokers: Up to 4: name, title (optional), phone, email. Empty list shows placeholders.
_notes.map_options: Optional: site_fill, aerial_fill, aerial_shift_pt, location_zoom, location_label_side, comps_label_side, pin_radius_m (framing when no parcels).
_notes.skip_aerial: Optional true: drop the Overhead Aerial page (leased sites).
_notes.lease_mode: Leased sites: pricing = {mode: 'lease', ask/trade = $/RSF/yr, ask_label: 'Suggested Asking Rent', trade_label: 'Expected Achievable Rent'}, comps_title = 'Recent Lease Comps', disclaimer = lease wording, comp_fields e.g. [City, Lease Date, SF Leased, Rent/SF/Yr, Lease Type, Term, Year Built, Notes].
_notes.lease: Written by scripts/lease_to_json.py from the lease workbook: as_of, summary_rows, notes, opinion, pf_rows, pf_total, pf_note. Adds Lease Summary and Cash Flow Pro Forma pages.
_notes.comps_title: Optional page title for the comps pages (default 'Recent Sales Comps').
_notes.disclaimer: Optional replacement for the fee simple disclaimer on the Market Value page.
_notes.cover_photo: Optional: image file (or {src, focus: [x, y]} as 0-1 fractions) for the cover. Cropped to the frame around the focus point and saved at 300 dpi; replaces the cover placeholder. Optional 'note' adds a small caption in the photo's bottom-right corner (e.g. 'Approximate rendering; current photography not readily available.'). Optional 'zoom' (e.g. 1.4) crops tighter so the building fills more of the frame; placed resolution drops by the same factor.
_notes.intro_photo: Optional: same format, for the full-width photo band on the intro page (792 x 327 pt). Replaces the intro_photo_note placeholder.
_notes.skip_value: Optional true: drop the Market Value page (leased sites). The Lease Summary page then carries the lease opinion and the disclaimer.
_notes.traffic_counts: Optional list for the Overhead Aerial: {road, vpd, year, lat, lon, side: right|left|up|down, width}. Place lat/lon on the road itself; points outside the frame pin to the edge with an arrow. geom.json 'map' holds the transform to convert aerial page points back to lat/lon.

intro: At your request, Cresa has prepared a Broker Price Opinion (BPO) for 13550 South Gessner Road in Missouri City, Texas, considering current market conditions, property-specific characteristics, and recent comparable sales of warehouse and industrial facilities across the greater Houston market.

The Subject Property is an approximately 29,325 SF Class B industrial warehouse on roughly 1.76 acres (76,666 SF) fronting South Gessner Road just north of US 90A in Missouri City. Built in 2011, the single-tenant building includes approximately 4,725 SF of office and 24,600 SF of warehouse space with 26-foot clear height, three drive-in doors, one exterior dock, fire sprinklers, and heavy 1,600-amp, 460-volt three-phase power on a fenced site. The property is currently occupied by its owner, Waterworld USA Inc, and for this analysis is assumed to be delivered vacant at sale.

The purpose of this report is to provide an estimated fair market value of the fee simple interest, assuming vacant delivery, based on current market conditions, expressed as a range from a suggested asking price to an expected trade value, supported by maps, parcel data, and comparable market data. This opinion was prepared without an on-site or interior inspection; land and building information is based on CoStar, Fort Bend Central Appraisal District (FBCAD) records, and information provided by ownership. This opinion is not a certified appraisal.

location_text: The Subject is located in Missouri City on South Gessner Road near Pike Road, within the Hwy 59/Hwy 90 (Alt) industrial submarket of Houston’s Southwest Corridor. The site sits about a half mile north of US 90A and less than a mile west of Beltway 8 (Sam Houston Tollway), with Interstate 69/US 59 roughly two miles to the northwest and downtown Houston about 14 miles to the northeast.

This positioning offers quick access to the Beltway 8 loop and Houston’s southwest freight routes, linking the Subject to Stafford, Sugar Land, and the broader region. South Gessner Road carries more than 32,000 vehicles per day at the site.

demographics.summary: The Subject sits in an established, growing trade area, with roughly 404,500 residents and 136,300 daytime employees within five miles and population projected to grow 1.8% annually through 2030. Median household income within one mile is $80,272, well above the wider area, and South Gessner Road carries more than 32,000 vehicles per day at the site.
demographics.source: Source: CoStar; 2025 estimates and 2030 projections. Traffic counts: CoStar, 2026.

narrative: The Hwy 59/Hwy 90 (Alt) submarket remains one of Houston’s stronger industrial markets, with vacancy of about 6% against a 7% citywide average, though conditions have softened in 2026 as new deliveries add supply. Small-bay vacancy has risen to roughly 5% but remains below the broader market. Recent sales of 46,000 to 80,000 SF buildings across southwest and northwest Houston traded between $136 and $162 per SF, with the new and high-clear product at 7711 Blankenship Dr and 7400 W Sam Houston Pkwy N at the top of the range.

The Subject’s 2011 construction, 26-foot clear height, heavy three-phase power, and fenced site near Beltway 8 align most closely with the 12701 Directors Dr and 5919 Bonhomme Rd trades at $136 to $139 per SF. Its smaller size supports pricing at or slightly above that range, while its limited dock loading and older vintage keep it below the $161 to $162 per SF achieved by newer product. We suggest an asking price of $4,200,000 ($143.22/SF) with an expected trade near $4,000,000 ($136.40/SF).
